Register a lazy tbl or dbMatrix/dbSpatial as a VIEW in the SQL Rooms database

Source: R/launchBrowser.R
sqlrooms_register.Rd

Creates a SQL `VIEW` (optionally `TEMPORARY`) over `x` in the connection associated with the current SQL Rooms session. No data is materialized: the view is a lazy alias that the SPA / `/api/arrow-query` can query.

Usage

sqlrooms_register(name, x, project = NULL, temporary = FALSE, overwrite = TRUE)

Arguments

name

Character. View name to create.

x

A lazy `tbl`, dbMatrix/dbSpatial, or data.frame.

project

Optional. A `dbProject` R6 object or `DBIConnection`. Defaults to whatever was passed to [launchBrowser()].

temporary

Logical. Create a `TEMPORARY VIEW` (default `FALSE`). Persisted (non-temporary) views are written to the database file and are visible to the SPA after the next page reload.

overwrite

Logical. Use `CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW` (default `TRUE`).

Value

Invisibly, a `dplyr::tbl()` pointing at the new view, or `TRUE`.

Details

Accepted inputs: - `tbl_lazy` / `tbl_sql`: rendered via `dbplyr::sql_render()`. - `dbMatrix` / `dbSpatial` (or any S4 with a `[]` extractor returning a `tbl`): the underlying lazy tbl is extracted via `x[]`. - `data.frame`: forwarded to [sqlrooms_export_table()] (materializes).

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
library(dplyr)
tbl(con, "cells") |>
  filter(x > 0) |>
  sqlrooms_register("cells_pos", x = _)
} # }
